correctness.rationale: The quotient map from the triangular tessellation has deck lattice L_n={(a,b):a+3b is 0 mod n}, with basis (-3,1),(n,0). The triangular-lattice word norm is max(|a|,|b|,|a-b|). For n>=17 every kernel endpoint reachable in at most four steps satisfies a+3b=0 exactly; exhaustive six-step-alphabet classification shows no nonzero endpoint through length three and only ±(-3,1) at length four. This yields exactly the n consecutive four-cycles. Classes outside the systolic subgroup have |a+3b|>=n and therefore length at least ceil(n/4); explicit vectors in each residue class modulo four attain the bound by simple cycles.

value.rationale: This is an infinite-family structural theorem rather than a finite census. It shows that a rank-two torus homology group can have an absolute shortest shell supported entirely in one primitive direction while the shortest independent direction grows exactly as ceil(n/4). The widening 4 versus ceil(n/4) gap quantifies strong combinatorial anisotropy in a natural published vertex-transitive family.
